brief: Following a stronger-than-expected payrolls report last week, today's PPI and tomorrow's CPI are framed as pivotal to expectations for the Sept. 15-16 FOMC meeting. Higher energy prices should lift the headline prints, but the Fed watches core measures. The bank expects core CPI to ease to 2.4% YoY, reinforcing that inflation is cooling rather than broadening and giving the Fed confidence to hold rates steady. Separately, amid rising oil prices and yields the S&P 500 has gained under 1% since end of May, compressing its forward PEG ratio to 0.8x, the lowest since 2008. Despite expected near-term volatility, the bank stays constructive on US equities over the next 12 months on fundamentals, secular growth, and more compelling valuations. Brent closed above $100 a barrel for the first time since July 23 amid a Persian Gulf flareup. Overseas natural gas has spiked more than oil, with Asia's JKM up 157% YTD and Europe's TTF up 182% YTD, while US Henry Hub gas is down 24% YTD, easing the burden for US consumers. Also noted: Macy's raised guidance, Oracle, Adobe, RH and Kroger report this week, and Fidelity data show 401(k) balances up 10.5% to $156k as loan-carrying savers rose to 19.5%.
